chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Ya'qub ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ali, on the authority of Ibn Ziyad, on the authority of al-Halabi that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Three things for which God will not question a believer: the food he eats, the clothes he wears, and a good wife who helps him, and guards his chastity.

key_terms.يُحَاسِبُ: to call to account or question

ai.seo_question: What three things will God not question a believer about according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of *khaff al-hisab* (lightening of the reckoning) for believers, emphasizing that mundane necessities like sustenance, clothing, and marital relations are exempt from strict scrutiny when utilized for lawful purposes. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly view that the world is not inherently opposed to faith, but rather a means of worship when one guards their chastity and fulfills domestic responsibilities, thereby transforming daily acts into spiritual merits.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-2 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali, on the authority of Ibn Zyad, on the authority of Al-Halabi that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
There are three things which God will not question a believer about: the food he eats, the clothes he wears, and a good and helpful wife who helps him, and assists him in guarding his chastity.”
